note: Set A states the cooking mass thresholds, the 96 oz starting-water minimum, linear scaling, and the village/neighborhood counts with correct values, units and supporting quotes, and makes no misbindings. Set B adds the reduced-range upper bound and two readings of the Figure 9 curve, but binds three scoring thresholds to the entity "kitchen appliance" and supports its two graph claims only with axis-label quotes that say nothing about the trend. Both sets heavily duplicate the same mass thresholds restated in lb/oz/kg, and both omit several dinner-party facts (two parties per team, eight-person guest list, 0–100% score range, 11 p.m. deadline, nine scores averaged). A is the cleaner and more faithful set overall.
remarks: Both extractors expand each mass threshold into up to five near-identical claims (5.000 lb / 80.00 oz / 2.268 kg / >=80 oz / >=2300 g); unit variants of one fact should be collapsed. B's two "points trend" claims (constant 0 points below 16 oz, linear increase 16–80 oz) are consistent with the plotted curve in Figure 9, but their quotes are only the axis labels "Points per cooking task vs Weight of vaporized water (oz)", which do not support them. Facts on the page that neither set captures: two dinner parties per team, guest list limited to eight people (two per neighboring house plus up to two VIPs), percentage integer scores ranging 0%–100% submitted by 11 p.m., nine scores averaged and multiplied by maximum available points, the requirement that the kitchen appliance operate in its normal configuration, and the lighting-exception/dimmer provisions at the top of the page. Note also the internal inconsistency in the source itself (0.454 kg vs 450 g, 2.268 kg vs 2300 g) which both sets reproduce faithfully.
